simple: Running exactly the same program, test and recording once in the simulator and once on the real machine, so the two recordings can be laid side by side.
analogy: Riding the same route on the trainer and on the road, with the same cycle computer recording both rides.
precise: Two executions of one controller build and one test plan (sequence, gains, limits, scenario) against two worlds behind the same hardware interface, each writing a log with identical columns and a run record; only the world and its conditions may differ, which the comparison tool checks before comparing.
source: R1, R2 of BR-08 (runs in this build, stand-in kit)

simple: The lines at the top of a log that say how the test was done: which machine, which program, which settings, in what conditions.
analogy: The line in a ride diary that says which bicycle, which tyre pressure and what the weather was.
precise: The header of a log naming the world, conditions, controller, gains, period, calibration parameter, filter settings, scenario and how the run ended; a measurement without it cannot be compared or repeated.
source: R4 of BR-08 (run in this build); C2 of BR-08 (curriculum 19.4 log entry template)

simple: Things the real machine does that the simulator does not contain at all, not even with a wrong number.
analogy: The school bicycle never pulled to the left, so practice on it never taught how to correct for that.
precise: States, nonlinearities or couplings of the physical system with no counterpart in the model's structure (for example dry friction modelled as an input deadband, a driver current limit, a once-per-revolution disturbance); identifying parameters cannot remove them, only a change of model structure can, and they show as a residual that stays after the parameters are right.
source: D2 of BR-08 (pending verification); R3 of BR-08 (run in this build)

simple: Deliberately gentle controller settings for the first runs on new hardware.
analogy: Riding the first laps at walking pace.
precise: Controller gains chosen for a large stability margin, so that the loop tolerates several times the delay expected on the hardware; used until the hardware's own delays and parameters are measured, after which gains are raised from the identified model one step per run.
source: R5, R9 of BR-08 (runs in this build); D1 of BR-08 (pending verification)

simple: Checking the robot's own speed reading against a separate instrument before trusting it.
analogy: Riding next to a friend whose cycle computer you know is right.
precise: A short closed-loop hold at a low setpoint on the bench in which the measured quantity is compared with an external reference that does not pass through the software's calibration parameters; the sequence continues only if the ratio is within a tolerance written down beforehand.
source: R6 of BR-08 (run in this build, stand-in kit)

simple: A rule in the software that refuses to drive the motors until the safety checklist says it may.
analogy: A grown-up's hand on the saddle: no riding until it is there.
precise: A decision function between a request to drive motors (motor test, closed loop on the bench, flight) and the outputs, evaluated against the signed bench record (propellers off, e-stop tested, supervision, rules recorded); it adds to the hardware emergency stop and never replaces it.
source: R7 of BR-08 (run in this build); C1 of BR-08 (guide safety rules)

simple: A pretend kit, written as a program, that plays the real kit when no real one is available.
analogy: A practice partner who imitates the road's bumps so the plan can be rehearsed.
precise: A teaching model of motor, battery, driver, encoder and clock with invented values (BR-08's kit_model.hpp), used in place of hardware to exercise the method; it proves nothing about any real kit and is replaced by the kit's own hardware interface on the bench.
source: R1 of BR-08 (run in this build)
